Quote: Guest, 2004-04-13T17:38:06Z
one of the rules is, if you hit something which accelerates you (like the jumppads), then any part of your velocity which is pointed AGAINST this acceleration is cancelled. so for instance, if you're moving right and hit a right-pointing jumppad, you'll still preserve your inertia. but if you run into it while moving left, your left-inertia will be cancelled.

without this rule things were a lot less fun; for instance when you were moving fast downward, jumps didn't move you up -- they only slowed your descent

See, it seems like it would be more fun if you went HIGHER off an upward jump pad if you hit it with some downward acceleration. So if you jumped onto a jump pad you would actually go much higher than if you just stepped onto it.

Maybe you could add a separate object that reacts more like a trampoline than the current launchpad. Both objects would be useful in creating maps.

The current "jumpbox" would be a good model, only it needs to actually fling N back into the air when he lands on it, but only porportional to how hard he lands on it. And you should be able to live from any height if you land on the "trampoline".

Normally when you die, you get to start that level over with all the time you had when you first started.

In broiler mode, you don't. You must complete the whole episode, and death equals a permanent loss of time.

I think you will see a greater variety of scores with that style of scoring.

Take for instance the first episode, where EVERYONE is going to be getting around 310 to 315, once they figure out all the cilantro tricks llcooldave used. There's no fun in that. But it would be much harder to have to do all the cilantro tricks on 5 consecutive levels.

#22679 7 2004-04-29T19:43:26Z Daddaluma
Quote: Guest, 2004-04-29T14:56:27Z
anyway, thanks for the ideas; our current plan is to have the following categories:

-highest 10 "remaining lifespans" for each episode
-highest 10 "amount of gold collected" for each episode
-lowest 5 times for each level

I would expect to see a *very* high correlation between these categories. Meaning, that whoever collects the most gold the fastest will generally have the higher remaining lifespan. This is a direct result of the infinite retrys available to everyone.

Granted, on alot of the later levels, where basic survival is the huge concern, there will be a greater variety of scores.

So if you're not keen on the idea of losing all the time spent on a level that you die on, then you could add a death penalty, maybe even just 1 second per death. THAT would definitely add a ton of variety to the scores, because, while it's easy to get a near perfect run given an infinite amount of attempts, it won't be that easy when you're losing a second of time every time you retry.

For the puzzle solving aspect of the game, I like the infinite amount of retries, but in terms of highscores, death should have a penalty attached. And falling in tony Hawk DOES have a penalty attached. You lose the time it takes to get up and get going again, which could have been used for scoring more points. That's exactly what I'm suggesting should be implemented for this game.

Keep in mind that I'm suggesting an alternate high score list here. There would still be the regular one with no death penalty, so if you think a death penalty somehow makes the game too frustrating, you don't have to participate in that mode of play. It would be open to those who want the added challenge and enjoy it.

Once the high scores stagnate (and I'm almost positive they will at some point), there needs to be a way to renew the competition. This can be done with new levels, but it can also be done by adding a broiler highscore mode of play.

#38876 113 2004-12-01T06:36:30Z Daddaluma
I would suggest making the dwarves the "uncivilized" race. They shun technology, and befriend nature, not like the elves in the gay tree hugging manner, but more manly and gruff. The real outdoorsman race. They are at home with the animals. Many of the most reknowned and respected dwarves have been known to have wild mountain lion companions.

Their "cities" are more like very large gatherings of tents, and a a few larger more permanent stone or wodden structures. The people inhabiting these cities would be ever changing as the nomadic dwarves come and go as the please.

Naturally, being the extremem outdoorsmen they are, they are an extremely hardy race. Not bothered by harsh climates on both ends of the spectrum. They make all the tools they need out of the rocks the mountains provide, or from the skeletons left behind from their food.

Basically, take the opposite of the stereotypical elf (wise, silent, graceful, stealthy, pacisfist, eloquent, reserved, etc etc) and you have yourself a dwarf.

Anyway, there's my take on what you might want to do with the dwarf race. You have no real wildmen, american indian type races yet, and they could definitely make a flavorful addition to the world.
#38905 117 2004-12-01T14:51:24Z Daddaluma
Quote: Tsukatu, Dec 1 2004, 08:00 AM
Alright, I've decided to kind of pop my head in periodically, read the few latests posts, and comment if I have anything.
In this case, I do have something: a contrasting view of dwarves.
I might be alone, but I've always seen dwarves as the largest enemy to nature. Think about it this way...
Their mannerisms don't agree with nature. They're born in mountains (that's why they're so hardy, after all). Mountains produce dwarves. In those mines, they like to dig tunnels. Digging tunnels makes a race kind of buff and manly-like, which is what dwarves are. There's no particular advantage to height, so dwarves remained short (go Darwinism!). Being manly tends to build up testosterone, which contributes to more passionate anger and discrimination, in a mild sense. That is, they become short-tempered and impatient. When you think of a druid, you think of a patient, benevolent figure, right? What kind of dwarf will tolerate living in the forest? They're not patient enough, and they don't need their manliness and buffness to survive at all. Beyond that, dwarves like to mine things and dig tunnels and bang on pieces of metal with other pieces of metal. Where can you do any of that in a forest?
You're describing an elf, with all that forest business. If you put a human in a forest, you get an elf. If you put a human on a mountain, you get a dwarf. It's really that simple.
"Roughing it," eh? I call that a Wood Elf. Do you know how buff those guys are? (+2 Str, +2 Dex, -2 Con, -2 Int, -2 Cha, for those of you who play DnD) You don't need resilience and toughness to last in the forest, you just need to be able to kill things around you, while dwarves need to endure harsh climate and long work hours.

Do we have an official name for the snakepeople yet? From random descriptions I've seen above, they look like a yuan-ti... or if we want a simpler term, we have something extremely close to it in another system. In the glorious land that is Rokugan, we call those things Nagas. It's just easier to refer to them that way. Of course, in Rokugan, they're also about 3 times the size of a human and at least that many times as strong, but we can still call 'em what they look like.

Was this aimed at my suggestion for the dwarves?

I don't see any other likely target, so I'm assuming it is.

Anyway, I said nothing about dwarves living in a forest. Our views on dwarves really don't contrast at all except on one small issue: I was going for the mountain men/beastmaster angle for the dwarves, and abandoning the steroetypical "dwarves dig tunnels and carve stone and that's it" sort of deal they usually get.

But all the rest seems perfectly in line with what I had suggested.

Unless I missed something. Which is possible, cause it's late and I'm tired.

#42338 40 2004-12-25T05:47:27Z Daddaluma
@Brickman

My second one. This is of course a subjective category, but here is how I broke it down.


Creative points in Sammage's demo:

Jumping through the mines at the end. That's it, but it surprised the heck out of me, and I think it looks cooler than tktktk's version. It won me over because I definitely hadn't even thought about doing that. I just looked at the two side entrances and said "impossible, forget about it". When someone does something I didn't think could be done, I'd consider that really creative.


Creative points in my demo:

Jumping off the thump. This is somewhat difficult to do, and it's a huge time saver, and not exactly obvious, in my opinion. While others did it too (tktktk) I was the first.

Getting the exit switch with one jump. Another big time saver and not immediately obvious thing to do.


Creative points in tktktk's demo:

Jumping off the thump. Although, since I did it first, I gave the credit to me, so I didn't count this that high.

Jumping through the mies at the end. This was again, a copy off sammage (maybe not originally, but based on who posted first), but it was also different, and still really cool.


Creative points in Brickman's demo:

Riding the mine up the shaft. Here is where some real subjectivity comes in. I had personally thought of doing that already, so it didn't surprise me at all. Also, it's not difficult to do at all, which is part of creativity (as stated in the rules), so it didn't really win many creativity points in my opinion.


So there's my defense of the creativity votes.

As for style and entertainment, yeah, tktktk's demo is easily arguably the first place. I went by the rules once again, and they extol highly fluid demos over all others, it seemed. And I sort of agree with that too. I thought that my single leap for the exit switch without even slowing down at all was more stylish than tktktk's ending. That's what made my decision.

#45871 5 2005-01-13T00:10:47Z Daddaluma
I would highly suggest a revision of the scoring categories.

Personally, since N is completely geared toward speed, the time category should be worth more than the other categories. I would say just double the amount of points each place receives (i.e. 10 for first, 6 for second and 2 for third).

Style and Entertainment should be second most important. Perhaps 1.5 times it's current amount of points.

Creativity should be fine the way it is.

Completion is a ridiculous category, and shouldn't be getting equal weight with the other categories. First of all, it's definition needs to be reqorked and very clearly stated so we don't have judges (maniac) voting for horribly incomplete maps. Also, this category is mostly useless unless the map creator specifically creates things to do that don't need to be done ot finish the map. Usually, going for all the gold will increase your score. Usually. There are of course times where it won't, and then this category has some merit, but not for every map. There also needs to be some set criteria for how to officially rank maps that are "fully" complete. However, any way I can think of is already covered by other categories (you could rank them by speed, but that is covered by time. You could rank them by how much you liked them, but that will usually be the covered by style and entertainment.)

So I suggest eliminating completion for maps that it serves no purpose on, and then on maps where it does serve a purpose make the points 3,2,1 for first, second and third. Or if the map is really difficult to fully "complete" then you can up the points in this category for that week. A set unwavering point total for this category just won't work because it's so map specific.



Also, I would suggest allowing people to change the 2 demos they submit right up until the last second of the contest. Each person can still have 2 entries, but they can improve upon their two entries as much as they want. This will remove the punishment for posting early in the week, and allow more of a competition (like on the high score boards) to take place.

#1991 1 2005-02-10T01:19:37Z Daddaluma
So, to start out, an explanation of determinism.

We will start with the dictionary definition: Determinism is the philosophical doctrine that every state of affairs, including every human event, act, and decision is the inevitable consequence of antecedent states of affairs.

What this means is that everything that is happening right now is 100 percent a consequence of what happened immediately before. And that chain will continue right on back as long as time itself.

Which means that 5 billion years ago, when presumably all that existed was just gasses and rocks and other inanimate stuff, the entire universe is governed completely by immutable physical laws of nature. So so the position, velocity, composition interaction etc. of everything that existed at that time is completely and 100 percent determined. There can be no deviance from what the laws determine.

Well, then naturally, we have a nice chain that will continue to lead right on up to today, tomorrow, and the rest of time. Which means that what you are doing right now was already set in stone by events that happened 5 billion years ago.

So, since you don't have the power to change the laws of nature, or the distant past, then you don't have any ability to change what you do right now either.

And, of course, if you don't have the ability to change what you do right now, how can you possibly think that you have free will?

Here's the argument in logical form jsut so you get an idea of what you have to argue against to save your free will (if you want to).

P= the distant past
L = the laws of Nature, whatever they may be.
F = the future

Determinism states P + L --> F (the arrow stands for "entail", so read the past plus the laws of nature entail the future)

So, the argument goes as follows

P+L-->F
P, and P is not up to you
L, and L is not up to you
therefore F, and F is not up to you.

If F is not up to you, then you do not have free will.

I thought determinism had been 'proven' wrong. Quantum mechanics messes the whole deal up. Uncertainty in particles means you will never know how they will act at any point in time, regardless of the past and Newton's laws.

I have two points to make about quantum stuff.

One. To the best of my understanding of the uncertainty principle, all that it tells us is that it is impossible for us to calculate both the spin and the position of particles.

That does not mean that each particle doesn't actually have a definite spin or a position at a given time, and furthermore that doesn't mean that it's seemingly random and unpredictable movements aren't actually governed by set physical laws that we just don't know about.

And #2. Even if particles can move about in completely unpredicatable and random ways, then it doesn't save your free will.

If the only way in which there can be multiple possible paths for the future to take is for particles to randomly do one of two different things, then we are still not free.

Let me explain.

Randomness is the complete opposite of free will. If an action is random it is completely unfree. So, yes, if truly random things do occur, then it is actually possible that you will drink orange juice instead of coffee tomorrow morning, but it wouldn't be because of a free choice that you made, it would be because of complete and utter unpredictable randomness.

So, that said, I propose that quantum schtuff be left out of this discussion because it is very poorly understood by even quantum scientists, let alone us laymen.

#50343 41 2005-02-14T02:25:05Z Daddaluma
So, a few points to make.

Determinism isn't really the same thing as "predetermined". Predetermined has a sense of all things being destined to be the way that they are, as if something outside of natural physics has set the course of things.

Whereas determinism just states that the current state of affairs is a natural logical consequence of the previous. So really, this "time slice" is the direct and inevitable result of the previous "time slice". It just happens that that previous time slice was the direct and inevtiable consequence of the next previous "time slice".

There's nothing mysterious about it. You can just follow the causal chain back forever.

So, once again, what this all means is that once you have a starting point, which can be any time slice from before humans were around, then my initial argument will go through to its conclusion.

Some of you are saying that your actions are based on your choices. You are completely right. My point is, though, that at the time you made the choice, the other options available to you were illusory. It was not physically or metaphysically possible for you to choose anything other than the option you in fact picked.

Where the problem lies for most of you is in the fact that the path always and necessarily follows your choices, and thus you still want to say that you have free will.

So, for ease of disscussion I will give an example and then bold the real question at hand.

You are deciding between drinking coffee and orange juice in the morning. You go with coffee, but you could have just as easily gone for orange juice, or so you think. Your choice of coffee could have been determined 100,000 million years ago. You couldn't have chosen the orange juice, no matter how easily you think you could have gone the other way. It's been set in stone by the laws of nature since 100,000 million years ago.

So, here's the question: If it's absolutely impossible for you to have chosen the orange juice, how can you say that you freely chose the coffee?

#51095 57 2005-02-21T00:20:20Z Daddaluma
So, I do believe that the argument i posted is pretty much inescapably airtight, with the exception of the final step (i.e. the "therefore you have no freewill" part).

As I pointed out before, the core of this problem lies in the question, "If you could have done other than you in fact did, then how can you say you freely did what you did?" This question clearly implies that for an action to be free, we have to have been able to do other than we did. It seems like a valid definition of free will, which is why the initial argument against free will holds so much force. It's easy to accept that you need to have been able to make other choices.

But I don't think that that is actually what's important for free will. Rather, I would define a free action in this way.

"If I had wanted to choose option 2, then I would have." Where option 2 is any option that you did not in fact choose.

If you can say this about a choice you made, then I contend that this is enough to make that choice a free one. It took me an entire semester to come around to this though. I was really convinced that if we actually cannot make the other choice, then that's really all that matters. I wouldn't have any of this semantic "would have" bullshit. It was "could have" or unfree for me.

But, if you think about it, this new "redefining" of free actions fits our normal usage perfectly. It rules out scenarios like being in the locked room as unfree, which it should. Even if you had wanted to leave the room, you wouldn't have been able to. It's locked. You can't freely choose to stay in a locked room. And it keeps in all the actions we would normally consider free, like deciding between coffee and orange juice.

It basically comes down to contraint. If a choice you made wasn't constrained, then it was free.

There you go. That's my take on this whole shindig.

#52659 8 2005-03-05T07:54:05Z Daddaluma
Not trying to be mean or anything, but it's really poorly written. There are sentences I like, but they are far overshadowed by the sentences that either grate on me or are just plain incorrect.

Quote
Was it not just moment ago I witnessed a man fall, knife pointing high out of his ribs?

"Knife pointing high out of his ribs" strikes me as very awkward and doesn't easily bring out a clear image. The wording makes it sound like the knife came from inside of him and the blade is jutting out from his ribs.

Quote
Yes, I wasnt delusional, I did see the man fall, and he did have a knife wedged in his now carcass

"Yes, I wasn't delusional" sounds awkward to me. It might just be me though. I know what you want to say, but "his now carcass" is not grammatically correct, and it doesn't sound right either. Also, and far less important, "I wasn't delusional, I did see the man fall" is a comma splice. It should be a period.

Quote
The answer wouldnt come for some moments, perhaps two or three,

This just sounds comical. Maybe that's intentional though. If it's not meant ot be funny, then lose the "perhaps two or three".

Quote
I turned and faced those three smiling faces, to find them attached to a neck and body


I know your trying to make the sentences interesting, but this wording just strikes me as awkward.

Quote
I looked at their clothes, clean suits, freshly pressed.  Small black lines ran up their slacks and suits, pinstripes I believed they are called.

I like this part. It's the first clear image you've given us.

Quote
As I looked down at my silhouette reflecting in their shoes.

I like this too.

Quote
It twisted over, with the heel being the load bearer of the leg.

This is just bad. Poorly phrased, and created absolutely no image of what's going on. I have no idea what "twisted over" means, and I have no picture of what this should look like or what's happening.

Quote
The smiles were gone on all but one face, and the one smiling was the only one still in his place.

This isn't terrible, but it's vague. It's sort of boring to read, and doesn't create the sharp vivid images that good writing is supposed to create.

Quote
I then finally stopped looking at the face, and looked past it to see two eyes staring at me.

Looked past the face to see eyes? Seems like awkward phrasing.

This is another boring sentence, especially as it doesn't go anywhere because the guy immediately looks away after this. No reaction, no description of the eyes or how he felt. Nothing. It makes this sentence a throw away sentence. And particularly in a story this short you really don't want any throw away sentences.

Quote
but this time I was not perfectly portrayed

Might just be a personal preference, but I don't like the wording. Feels wrong or awkward or something.

Quote
A drop of blood fell in my figures way


This is also really awkward. The phrasing you used takes away from the image your trying to convey. Otherwise, this would be a good part. A clear picture of the man seeing his image in his soon-to-be-killer's shoe, marred by blood. That's a good crsip image that you don't want fudged up with awkward phrasing.


Quote
I looked for its source, and found it not concealed.

Too many "it"s referring to separate things. The phrase "found it not concealed" is awkward. Sounds funny. It's distracting to read and blocks the reader from getting really into the story.

Quote
As the blood from his like dressed friends slid off its edge, I finally started to piece what had happened together.

If you use "its" in this way, the reader expects the "it" to be the subject that comes right after the comma. So, at the very replace "it" with an actual object. But even after that, the whole sentence is a bit confusing. There are too many objects cluttering up the sentence makign it hard to interpret immediately. You got "his" (and we haven't been using a "he" as a subject yet, so this "his" is unlcear), "it", "like dressed friends" (which isn't horrible, but is a bit awkward sounding), and then the real subject of the sentence, the narrator. Just too much going on in one sentence.

I've got a few style issues with the rest, but nothing really worth mentioning.

Overall, this is a confusing piece to read, and the tons of awkward phrases of word choices make it frustrating to read. It's just not very good.

I'm not really complaining that the story is not clearly laid out. It's cool to have a scene where the reader isn't quite sure what's going on and has to read very carefully to figure out what's going on. But even those sorts of stories or scenes have to be written with well constructed sentences.

#52951 23 2005-03-07T00:20:05Z Daddaluma
Just want to add a quote I just read in an article in the New York Times.

"Poetry may be in the eye of the beholder but clarity is less subjective."

This is my point. You seem to think that I'm critizing the poetical aspects of your writing. I'm not. Your writing is riddled with awkward unclear phrases and sentences. That's bad under any circumstance, regardless of the style of writing your going for.

Fragments don't have to sound awkward. Saying, "it's the style i was going for" is not an excuse for making sentences that are entirely unclear due to word choice or phrasing.

And, just to clarify my initial critique, I said "to me" a bunch just to make the criticism sound softer, less authoritarian. Pretty much the only time when I thought I might just have a personal problem with one of the sentences was when I said, "this might be a personal preference . . ."

One last thing. It's really hard to edit your own writing. You know what you meant and what the story should look like, so you think that your sentences are just perfect the way they are. If your story's gonna get any better, you're gonna have to trust your readers that are honest enough to point out where they see flaws. It would be a big mistake to just dismiss my criticisms as mere opinion that don't apply because I just didn't get the style you were going for.

So, while I don't agree with Brickman's tone, I do agree that this writing is just not that good, and I don't have much interest in reading further (unless of course you start showing an interest in actually trying to edit some of those issues I pointed out). So, I'm not gonna breakdown that second part like I did the first.

#2204 1 2005-03-14T00:46:26Z Daddaluma
They are both awesome Strategy RPGs.

I would very highly recomend both games, with the slight edge going to FFT. Although, Disgaea will be easier to get into and is probably more engrossing in the short term.

And as I mentioned in the Game Naming Game thread, Disgaea is the ultimate game for munchkins. It's possible to get all the best equipment and the highest stats before you even begin the storyline. It's probably even faster to just skip the storybattles if you're just going for as much power as possible in the quickest time possible.

I have 2 copies of Disgaea now. I couldn't suppress the urge to play it again, and now I'm in Japan with a Japanese PS2, so I had to pick up the game for a second time. It's so worth it.

As for FFT, I'm having a great time playing it on an emulator on my computer. It's a tad slow in this day and age, so the ability to ramp up the framerate and to save states is priceless. Also, playing it on a computer gives you easy access to your memory cards and savegames, so you can cheat like crazy, or try all those cool things that you wanted to before but couldn't (like play through the game with just Ramza as an Assassin). You can also skip all the boring parts (like doing random battles to gain experience and JP).

So there you go. Play them both. They'll both offer you literally hundreds of hours of gameplay (and if you're insane, possibly thousands of hours).

#2278 1 2005-03-23T04:21:46Z Daddaluma
So, I was unable to make a new topic for about 10 minutes there.

After some research on the adblock website and looking at the blocked elements on this page, I figured out that the filter *ads* blocks everything that contains those letters in that order.

That includes things like http://2.forumer.com/uploads/metanet/post-12-1105770822.gif

But adblock doesn't just not let you see the stuff. It actually gets rid of it. So I couldn't even make a new topic to ask about how to get around all this crap.

So I went digging on the adblock forum and found a little bit of adblock code that I don't understand but worked: /[^a-zA-Z]ads*/

That apparently restricts the filter to only things that exactly match "ads".

Solved my problem.

Anyway. Just wanted to share my little adventure.

Quote: Maniac, Apr 17 2005, 08:50 AM
I absolutely hate this level. After doing the new MetaNet columns, I still hate it.

What gave you the urge to hide stuff? It leads to horrible level-making.

Many users on NUMA rate down for hidden junk, and it really makes the level dumber, with newbie difficulty. Trial and error with hidden stuff isn't fun.

WHY, M&R, WHY?
Seriously, this all encompassing hate of "hidden objects" is ridiculous.

What's stupid is a hidden object where people have absolutely no idea it's there and it's guaranteed to kill you until you memorize where it is. For example thumps hidden in walls. Really annoying and pointless.

But 79-2? gimme a break. It's painfully obvious that there's something behind those bounce blocks. It's also obvious what you have to do to avoid them. There's no memorizing which block contains a switch and which contains a mine. Nothing stupid that requires luck or trial and error.

And there is really only one way to force people to do that quick jump off the bounce blocks, and that's hide an object underneath it.

So people giving out automatic 0s for hidden objects really annoy me. If the map is terrible, and uses hidden objects terribly, then fine, give it a 0.

But to just blanketly say "Hidden objects = the devil" is ignorant and childish. Get over it already. 79-2 is a fun level.

P.S. this is not aimed only at you, Maniac. This is aimed at everyone who's out of control with the hidden object hatred. You just happened to provide the perfect stimulus for my own mini-rant.
#60518 11 2005-04-18T13:42:09Z Daddaluma
Quote: Eli, Apr 18 2005, 08:48 PM
Not once have I seen a hidden object used well.

And no, you absolutely DO have to memorize things on 79-2.

79-2's main problem isn't that the stuff is hidden, though. It's the lag, the horrible confounded ever-present lag that drives you, unable to resist, into your doom within the blocks. It is the delay and irregularity on all your actions that prevents you from even jumping with consistency, that on this atrociously designed level plunges you even deeper into the Random Death Syndrome that is the bane of every game...

I'm not sure where this lag is coming from, but I don't have that problem.

And what exactly do you have to memorize in 79-2? That the two center ones have mines and not jump pads?

Everything beneath the blocks is bad and you don't want to hit it. That's the challenge. Oh noes, the middle ones contain instant death if you fail to quick jump. It took you what, one whole run to figure that out? Did that ruin your entire N experience because you died unexpectedly one whole time?

It's not the hidden objects that are bad. Nothing about hiding objects beneath bounce blocks is inherently bad. It's when you hide them in such a manner that requires a player to use trial and error to beat the level. That's not a test of skill, that's just stupid.

But 79-2 is a complete test of skill. You have to do your best to jump at the right moment repeatedly. I happen to find the level very fun, but I can see how the game lagging could make this level a true nightmare. However the game lagging isn't a function of the game. It doesn't lag for me. The most successful NTTS maps are relatively easy to beat. You don't want to have any week where it's too hard/frustrating to even beat the level that no one even bothers trying to compete on things like style and creativity.

A good NTTS map usually offers some freedom so people have a lot of choice in their routes and can be more creative. This is not set in stone of course. And it doesn't mean the level can't be linear or narrow or have an obvious path.

#65327 30 2005-05-13T02:36:46Z Daddaluma
Ok, here is a copy of the rules I just wrote up. If you've got major complaints, or there are typos, let me know.

Numa Time Trial Society (NTTS) Rules

For a complete overview of all things NTTS go to Kablizzys NTTS site. I will list any and all changes from those rules here.

This is basically a replay contest. We will have a new map to compete on every 2 weeks. Players will have a week and a half to come up with the best replays they can. We will be using the user levels option on the menu, so make sure you know how to properly play a level and save a replay. Because this function only records completed replays, we will only be accepting fully complete replays. No more replays where you die in cool ways or anything like that.

Each person will be allowed to submit 2 replays. If you choose to submit your two replays early in the week, you may still submit replays later on to take the place of the earlier ones.

If you do decide to submit a new replay in place of an old one, please make a new post with the new replay and delete the old replay from your old post. The order of submitted replays will make a difference in the judging. There is likely going to be a great deal of strategy involved in submitting your replays. So take a moment to think about whether its a good idea to submit your killer replay right away or to hold off until later in the week.

So, once the week and a half is up, and we have all the replays in, the three judges will begin to watch them and rank them. Previously we had the judges rank the best three replays in 4 separate categories. This season were going to try something different. There will still be a Time category with 3 places receiving 5, 3 and 1 points. This will not require judging. One person can win only one slot even if both their demos are faster than anyone elses.

Then the judges will rank the top 5 best replays. The judges may use whatever criteria they like to rank them. 1st place could be the fastest and most stylish replay whereas 2nd place could be a replay where someone pulled off a really cool stunt that no one else did. Its entirely up to the judges discretion. The ranks will be averaged and the winner will be determined from that. There will be 5 places receiving 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 points.

A single person can win more than one spot if both of their demos are different enough and still spectacular. It will be up to the judges to decide.

Your judges will be:

trib4lmaniac
Nevermore
Daddaluma

If for some reason a judge cannot fulfill his duties then our alternate, jeffkillian will take over for the week.

Edit: I've officially reached a blistering posting rate of 1 per day That's a far cry from the .6 I used to be at

#73676 12 2005-06-10T06:16:31Z Daddaluma
A lot of you seem to be misunderstanding the idea. This phrase is only used when you do some bad stuff to achieve a greater good.

So Brickman's example "If you have to kill somebody to get home in time for your aniversary" is ridiculous. This is not what the phrase applies to.

LV's example is a good one (albeit quite an extreme one). Would you personally push the button that would instantly slaughter 2 billion people if you knew it would save the rest of the people and the earth?

More examples. The police strongly suspect that they have captured a terrorist involved in plot to launch a nuclear missile at the US. THey torture their captive for hours until he gives up and reveals what he knows and it leads to the successful thwarting of the attack. Do the ends justify the means? (thank you 24)

Another one: research suggests that violent tendencies may be genetically linked. The government institutes a policy of sterilizing all humans who are convicted of violent crimes. In a few generations we see a large decrease in the number of such violent crimes. Do the ends justify the means? What if we changed "sterilized" to "executing"? (thank you eugenics)


These are the kinds of questions you should be thinking about. Any idiot can come up with a scenario where obviously the ends don't justify the means, that's not what you should be thinking about.

How about one last one. The human race is seperated into alphas and betas. Alphas live their lives however they want. They can choose their jobs and pursue whatever liveliehood they'd like. Betas are like slaves. They do all the dirty work. Manual labor, janitorial all the tough crappy jobs that have to be done but most people don't really desire to do.

The catch is that the betas are fed a drug called "soma" which makes them extremely happy and satisfied with their lives.

So everyone is happy with the arrangement. Normal people (alphas) live in a much easier and cleaner environment and the betas live long and fulfilled lives due to the soma.

Do the ends justify the means? (thank you Brave New World)

Edit: I just reread Keron's post, and it seems that he specifically said that he wasn't talking about the kind of huge issues I just brought up. But the general point still applies. The ends can only justify the means if the ends do a greater good than the means do harm, but even then you'll run into a bunch of ethical questions which are fun and important to think about.

Edit 2: added credit to where it's due in my examples

#76567 80 2005-06-20T00:34:55Z Daddaluma
There are some very good reasons for pot to be made legal that have nothing to do with it's merits as a medicine.

http://con.ca/issues/5/15/166

This article generally goes over a large amount of the reasons why marijuana shoulnd't be illegal. Granted shouldn't be illegal isn't quite the same thing as should be legal, but if it shouldn't be illegal, then what else is there besides being made legal?

Anyway, aside from the reasons in the article, there are a few more really good ones.

I will highlight the relevant portions, but for reference here is where I got my numbers: http://www.mpp.org/arrests/fas61699.html

Quote
Totals and Costs
Adding the jail and prison estimates gives a total of 59,300 people incarcerated for marijuana offenses. Using the adjusted estimates for "marijuana only" gives a jail-plus-prison total of 37,500 people incarcerated for marijuana without any other drugs involved. (To be even more precise, this figure ought to be adjusted to reflect the fact that the "lead charge" reflected in the Survey of Inmates may not be the only, or even the primary, reason a person is in prison; the data does not tell us whether this adjustment would, on balance, be up or down.) Finally, using the adjusted estimates for possession gives a jail-plus-prison total of 15,400 people incarcerated for possessing only marijuana.

At an average annual cost per prisoner-year of more than $20,000,[8] the total cost to taxpayers of marijuana-related incarceration reaches more than $1.2 billion per year. (This does not include the cost of investigating, arresting, and prosecuting the hundreds of thousands of marijuana users arrested every year.)

Or then there's this site: http://www.doctordeluca.com/Library/WOD/Cr...ion-NORML05.htm

Which includes all the costs of arrests and courts costs and puts the final estimate of cost of trying to battle marijuana users at over 7 billion dollars per year.

That's 7 billion dollars that could be freed up immediately if we simply made marijauna legal right now.

But further than that, the government could regulate, tax and sell marijauna, turning that 7 billion dollar money sink into a who-knows-how-many-billions profit.

Not to mention the amount of people that would be freed from prison opening up some much needed space for real criminals.

These are real reasons why marijauna should be at the very least decriminalized.

If you're worried about the increase in irresponsible use of marijauna, then we could use a few of those billions of dollars freed up toward providing actual drug related education and free rehabilitation centers and such. Things that would go alot further to deterring the use of drugs than draconian prison sentences do.

Because if the universe can't come from nothing then god can't just poof into existence either. If we need a creator, its only logical that he does (especially because if he's perfect then he would need even MORE careful tinkering than anything he made).

No. You're failing to comprehend what "perfect" actually means.

If God is perfect then he can't have any attribute that implies a lack or the possibility of something greater. There can be nothing greater than something perfect. It's a logicial impossibility.

If God were to need creating, well then that's a lack of perfection right there. A Perfect being cannot have been created at any point by necessity. If you're able to think of something greater than a perfect being, then obviously that being was never perfect to begin with.

#4304 1 2005-09-05T12:29:16Z Daddaluma

MMMMMYou rub your eyes groggily as you slowly rise out of slumber. Its funny, you dont recall ever actually going to sleep. The bright light makes it difficult to open your eyes immediately and you blink gingerly, allowing your eyes a few minutes to adjust. When you finally manage to get a good look at your surroundings your body freezes as a wave of panic floods over you.

Where the hell am I?


MMMMMYou find yourself on the floor in a gigantic room, the size of a large warehouse. The ceiling is at least 30 meters above your head and there are innumerable large fluorescent lights beating down on you. As you forcefully hammer down the panic trying to well up inside, you notice the inordinately large amount of doors. There must be at least 100, maybe more. An enormous digital clock attached high up on the far wall reads 10:23:57:27, the last number counting down in 1 second intervals.

MMMMMUpon further inspection you notice a number of others scattered about the room coming to in a similar fashion. They look vaguely familiar, but you cant put your finger on why or where you think you might have seen them before. From the looks on their faces you surmise that theyre in the same boat as you, completely bewildered, without a clue as to where you are or how you got here.

MMMMMBefore you can talk to anyone, or even get to your feet, you see one crazed young boy dash toward the nearest door. You think you can just make out a number 84 painted on it, but its too far away to be sure. Without warning or hesitation, the youth turns the door-knob and pulls. For a split second relief washes over you as nothing happens. Maybe the door is locked or stuck or something. But a moment later the door gives way with a loud creak and begins to open.

MMMMMA sense of dread, immediate and profound, grips you tightly. It probably grips the guy who opened the door too, but it is too late for him. His body is engulfed in a fiery flash that instantly incinerates him, leaving only a cloud of ashes to float gently to the floor.

MMMMM The shock of what just happened doesnt sink in right away. It was too sudden and too unbelievable to take it all in. You and the others look around at each other looking for answers in each others eyes, but no one has anything to offer. Everyone is just as perplexed as the next guy. The same thought thunders through our head once again, this time much more intense.

Where the hell am I?!



MMMMMIf you wish to participate, these are the guidelines.


MMMMM - You are you. You dont have any powers you dont have in real life. If youre 12, then youre 12 in the game. If youre 35, then youre 35 in the game.

MMMMM - You cannot make up anything at all about the game world. Go on what I give you. If you want more detail, then youll have to have yourself do some searching around. Ill tell you what you see and then you can further choose to interact with whatever you find or see.

MMMMM - If there is stuff that everyone can know just by looking around from their starting spot, I will post that here, so everyone can see. If your character goes snooping around by him/herself then I will PM results that should be known only to your character.

MMMMM - In general, real world physics applies with one general exception: All conversations players have with other players can somehow be heard by everyone, no matter how low they whisper and no matter how far away they are. So if you want to keep a secret, you have to keep it from absolutely everyone. If you tell one person, you tell them all. You can, however show someone something, in which case only they could see it. Youll probably want to do that through me.

MMMMM - If youre going to play, then please post a short bio of yourself. Just some simple statistics will help. Age, weight, height. General physical characteristics, are you athletic? Do you really like math? Etc. etc. (I suppose you could lie if you really wanted to, and no one would know). No need to go super in depth at all. It might not have any bearing on anything, but then again, it might. So, whatever you want to tell me.

MMMMM - You can all feel free to talk to each other at any time. Share what you know. Whatever you want. But if you want to do something other than interact with the other players you have to do it through me.

Feel free to ask all the questions you have as I havent completely thought up everything myself yet. The game has not started yet, so dont go interacting with each other just yet. Don't ask about the storyline though, stick to question about the mechanics of the game.

Im not quite ready to start this yet, so just be patient for a day or two. I was just looking to gauge interest with these signups. A lot more people than I expected have shown up . . . I might have to rethink a few things. For instance, if I run this thing by myself the way I had intended, then things will be slow going as I have to pretty much engage 1 on 1 with every single player. Going slowly isnt necessarily a bad thing though, so I may stick with that.

When the game starts you will be given a whole host of information about the room, whats in it. I might even work on a small diagram so people have a visual representation. Until then, no need to ask question about air ducts and such. After I give out the starting info, if theres still stuff you want to know about the room, have your character do some in depth searching and Ill post results. If theres stuff that requires in depth searching and you happen to discover it, Ill let you know by PM. But if you are searching for air ducts and I realize I probably should have mentioned them in the first place to everyone, then I might just post results of your search into this public thread. Hopefully that made sense.

Im working out how the game should run right now. I think a lot of it will be learn by doing though.

For now, lets all assume that none of you wake up with any sort of supplies at all, other than the clothes on your back. Even if you happened to be carrying a 5 inch knife at the time you signed up, you dont have it when you wake up in the room.

For an example of how I envision this working heres a sample series of posts that could take place (grossly shortened for time and space concerns):

Maniac: Im going to search the north east corner. Im also going to place my ear on the wall and knock in several places to see what happens.

Daddaluma (in a pm to Maniac): over the course of your search you notice that there appears to be a brick loose on the bottom row. It looks as if you could pry it out if you had the right tools.

The brick wall does not produce any noticeable differences in any spot when you knocked on it.

Maniac: I found a loose brick here! I think we could pry it out. Does anyone have a knife or something we could use?

Red reamer: That crazy guy in the house over there gave me a knife a little while ago. Maybe we could use that? Im going to try to pry the brick loose.

Daddaluma (in a pm to Maniac and Red Reamer): The brick comes out with little fanfare. Behind it lies what appears to be a steel wall. You can just barely make out an engraving that looks to have been scratched into the steel wall many years ago. It says . . .



Get the idea?

I imagine that lots of people will be wanting to do lots of things at the same time, so the game progression could be slow. Also, Im in Japan, so my hours of operation are likely to be different that most of yours.

Anyhow, if youve got any more questions as to how a certain scenario might work or maybe you see problems I havent thought of, feel free to post them here. Im gonna get back to work planning things out.

GUIDELINES

#98335 2 2005-09-07T10:25:18Z Daddaluma
MMMMM After a minute or two your senses return and the paralyzing fear and shock subsides just enough for you to regain control of yourself. The dreadful events took place so rapidly that you question whether they even happened at all. The sheer absurdity of the situation prevents any sort of sadness or sympathy from welling up inside you. You feel almost completely separate from this reality in which you find yourself an unwilling resident.

MMMMM As the gigantic red digital numbers of the clock display continue their lifeless countdown, you begin to take notice of your surroundings a little more clearly. The room youre in is truly enormous. Bigger than you even realized at first. It must be half a kilometer long and nearly as wide. There are doors lining three out of the 4 walls. There must be at least a hundred of them, all the same bland modern style door you might find in every office building anywhere. Each of the 4 walls is made of a different material, brick, plywood, plaster (which you note seems to fit in perfectly with the office door theme), and concrete. All of the walls, save the one made of brick, are in disrepair, with large chunks either discolored or falling apart. The room is almost perfectly empty except for a shoddily constructed shack of sorts built up next to the only wall without doors.

MMMMM You begin to struggle to stand up when you finally notice the floor, perhaps the oddest part of the whole room yet. Youre standing on a brilliantly crafted tile floor. The arrangements, patterns and quality of workmanship are all masterful. But stranger yet is that it only a few yards away the floor is an excellent hardwood, and the two seem to blend into each other perfectly. As you ponder this oddity you spin around and realize that across the entire room the floor is comprised of totally random patches made of different materials. You can see stone, concrete, bamboo, even what looks to be a patch made up entirely of legos.

Quote: blue_tetris, Sep 15 2005, 04:03 PM
Blue

===========

Blue speaks primarily in the direction of Emma and Bud, but to the entire group as well.

"I don't mean to be getting upset, guys, but... bear with me.  Not helping us is getting you nowhere.  I believe, in life-and-death situations, the end justifies the means.  If we run around like tenacious like mice and scurry frantically and look silly... and we don't die, that means our running around wasn't so foolish after all.  If we make holier-than-thou observations and direct spiteful attitudes towards one another... and we die, then it doesn't matter how cool we thought we were while living... because we'll be dead."

"Now, I don't know how cool it must feel to withhold life-saving evidence and I'm not here to accuse anyone of doing that.  But if we die, we're dead.  Okay?  Dead.  And it doesn't matter how much fun you had in the meantime, because you won't get to look back upon it.  You'll be dead."

Blue speaks more softly and more rationally than before.

"Sorry.  I... I just got a little upset.  I know no one here wants to get anyone else killed.  I just want everyone here to be safe.  I want you, Emma, to be safe."

Blue walks over to Emma and holds her hands in his, but doesn't look her in the face.
Emma
=====

Looking shocked and apalled, Emma opens her mouth to speak but is silenced as Blue continues.

Quote: blue_tetris, 2005-09-15T07:03:02Z

"Don't take me as being too forward, but you remind me of someone.  My girlfriend.  She died recently in a car crash and... and then I found myself here.  I was just about to give up and let myself die.  Hell, if I hadn't gotten put down here, I might have tried to do myself in.  But this place has taught me that there's something in every person worth saving.  That life, no matter how futile it seems, is always worth living.  Because you never know when you'll meet someone..."

Blue raises his head and looks her in the eyes.

"...who changes your life.  Emma.  I'm going to make sure you get out of here alive.  Even if it costs my life.  Just remember that."

Through the course of Blue's speech Emma's expression changes from disgusted to curiously intrigued to saddened and finally to shamed embarrassment. She lowers her eyes as soon as Blue met her gaze. Something in his words just cut right through her, making her feel deeply ashamed of herself. She opened her mouth to speak once again, but words wouldn't come out. She sputtered and began to cry softly. After a brief moment, but before anyone else could say anything to her she managed to whisper:

"Here. Take it. Take it and leave me alone. I don't want to talk to anyone anymore. I don't want to see anyone anymore. I don't want to live anymore."

Before Blue or anyone else could react Emma ran off with surprising speed. Even if anyone had been close enough to stop her, they wouldn't have been able to catch her anyway.

She ran toward door 66, a door she knew to be fatal. Without a moment's hesitation she grabbed the doorknob and opened the door. Her body flamed and disappeared leaving behind only a bland gray pile of ashes and a crowd of stunned onlookers.


Bud
=====


Bud looked on in shock as a wave of guilt slammed into him. He knew he had nothing to feel guilty about, but the intensity of the hatred he had felt toward Emma made him feel bad. She had wronged him. He knew that, but now she was dead. It felt somehow wrong to feel such intense rage toward someone who just killed themself. Bud, saying nothing, went back to sitting by himself in the corner and reflected on the situation and his emotions.


Archie
=====


Archie was furious, as was his usual first reaction when something he didn't like happened. He didn't particularly like Emma, but he didn't think she should die either. He blamed the first and only thing he saw fit to. Running in the direction of blue tetris, he said:

"You son of a bitch. You had to go and open yer mouth to her didn't ya? She didn't need your emotional baggage ya bastard. Now yer gonna get it. You killed Emma, I kill you!"

Archie was running toward blue tetris wielding his lead pipe like a broadsword. The sight of a midget running like a madman carrying a pipe for a weapon would have been highly comical if he wasn't seriously trying to kill someone. As it was though, Archie's legs were short and not built for speed, and he was quite far away from blue tetris. It would be at least a minute or two before he reached him."

"Righto. Door 93.

This is it, I guess. My moment to shine, or to fizzle, or whatever."

*I pull some plywood in front of the door, in the shape of a question mark. And I do the same in front of door 21.*

"Man, it's been nice knowing you guys. See you on the other side... of the building, of life, whatever. You've all been great."

*I then look away from everyone in the room, and into the lights in the ceiling.*

"Fuck you."


And here's the scene, as it would be viewed from above-
Me, walking across the varied floor towards door 93. Me, with one hand, I have a finger pointed up at the heavens- or the ceiling- or whatever authority there is that brought me here. And, with the other, I hover it over the doorhandle. With one finger up in the air and five just above the doorhandle, I grip and pull.


The clock reads 9:00:37:22 as The Daily Llama reaches for door 93. Bracing himself for the worst, he gingerly places his hand on the doorknob, shuts his eyes and pulls.

It takes a few seconds before he realizes that nothing has happened to him. He is still standing in the room completely harm free! He falls to his knees and lowers his head, exhausted from stress and overcome with joy and relief.

The others in the room are stunned. The door lies open! They did it! Though at terrible cost, they solved the rooms puzzles. A great cheer arises among the survivors. Though they dont know what will happen now, they are all filled with an incredible optimistic confidence. So many have perished before them trying to get where they now stand. Whatever happens, its got to be good.

After a few moments, The Daily Llama struggles to his feat and looks around the room. He saw the shining faces of all those still living. He remembered the faces of those that fell along the way. Reaching a hand up to his face he wiped away a single tear that had begun to roll down his cheek. Saying a silent goodbye to the small crown, he turned back toward the gaping door and looked in.

It was pitch black. There wasnt a single feature that he could make out in the darkness. How this blackness would lead to his freedom he didnt know, but he felt sure that this was the one and only way out of the room. Hesitating only a moment to gather his strength and composure, The Daily Llama took a measured stride toward the doorway and crossed the threshold with the second.

The onlookers saw him walk towards the opening, half expecting those hateful flames to appear out of nowhere and burn his body into ashes before he could. But not this time. They watched in slow motion as the tip of his hand first pierced the darkness, slowly followed by his arm, then his head and body, and finally they watched as the last bit of his foot disappeared into the black nothingness.

Before any of them could even open their mouths the ungodly intense lights up above shut off. They found themselves in the same perfect blackness that The Daily Llama had just entered himself. Again, before any of them could even cry out in fear they all felt their eyes grow very heavy. Within a few instants they all felt their heads swimming with fatigue and sleep, the strongest among them managing to fight it off for only a second longer than the rest. They could know it, but The Daily Llama was experiencing the same thing at the same time.

After what seemed like only a few seconds, the sensation wore off and The Daily Llama opened his eyes and bolted upright. His mind was still swimming from the experience, and at first glance he wondered where on earth the door had taken him. He raised his hand to rub his eyes and clear his head, trying to make sense of his strange new surroundings when it hit him; he was back in his own bed!

Each and every person who was trapped in the room all woke up at the same time, each of them shocked and overjoyed to be back home again. But, within a few minutes the memories of the room had begun to fade, such that they could no longer clearly remember the details, or even if it had really happened or not. With each passing second the experience felt more and more like some sort of horrible nightmare rather than something real. Indeed it was easier for the mind to accept if the whole thing had just been a dream after all. Within a few days the entire ordeal had faded completely from the memories of all the survivors. They each went on living their lives as if nothing had ever happened, blissfully unaware that elsewhere in the world, several families were rocked with grief at the inexplicable disappearance of their children or loved ones.

Yes. This is the end. If you've got questions or comments, please feel free to post em.

Any suggestions for what to include or not to include or what to do better for next time (if there is a next time, naturally).

Let’s start with this: http://www.raptureready.com/rr-planet.html

You can take the time to read through it if you like. I’m gonna highlight one passage in particular.

Quote
“Fitting the age of our world into the 6,000-year time frame would require disrupting our understanding of the speed of light, annual growth cycles, the erosion process, historical records of tectonic movement, rates of decay for radioactive atoms, climate patterns, the historical content of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, the freezing point of water, and a host of other processes.
It would be foolish to modify everything we know about how the physical world operates just to accommodate one single theory. I find the chasm between reality and the young earth theory too vast for any explanation to span. Even if one is kind enough to assume that the growth of coral was once 10 times faster than it is today, some reefs would still be more than 13,000 years old.”

You can continue to post your singular pieces of contrary evidence (no star explosions older than 6000 years?), and I will continue to think less and less of your arguing skills. It’s called a forest, stop looking at the trees.

The massively overwhelming portion of the evidence points toward an earth and a universe that is many thousands of times older than 6000 years. To argue against that bit is like trying to fit a square peg into a solid reinforced steel board without any holes at all.

Now, onto other things.

I don’t claim to know a whole lot about evolution and the intimate details it involves, but I’d really wish you stopped spouting off “facts” as if you’ve done years of research on the subject and can conclusively prove that everything you're saying is right.

There are problems with evolution theory. This is true. Anyone who has read anything about it at all will know that the theory isn’t perfect and can’t explain absolutely all the data we’ve collected. But it’s by far the best theory we’ve got right now. To destroy the theory of evolution, you need a better, testable theory to replace it. That’s how science works.

We don’t have any theory like that. We don’t even see the possibility of such a theory on the horizon. It’s all well and good to point out issues with the current theory, but don’t flatter yourself. You’re not pointing out anything new, and these theory-killer problems you're raising could never be enough to overturn the enormous mountain of evidence that supports the theory.

So, I’d appreciate just a bit of humility. You’ve said a couple of the most arrogant things I’ve heard in a long while ("Yeah, personally I think scientists have it all wrong about the lightyear distances in the galaxy. But I can't prove that." You can't be serious . . .). You’d do well to realize that you're in the company of a few other intellectual powerhouses besides yourself and not take such an authoritative dogmatic tone.

Perhaps you'd like to point us to some resources that support your arguments. Actually, reading back through your posts, I don't see a whole lot of points to begin with. Quote: Maniac, Feb 5 2006, 10:06 PM
But what if a sorcerer announces first? Then the real detective couldn't announce without looking like a sorcerer. Which is obviously a very bad thing, as we'd be stabbing ourselves in the spleen.
I already went over this in the first post.

If a sorcerer calims to be the detective first, then the real detective should also claim to be the detective.

Then we have a couple of options. Kill them both. As no villager in their right mind who is NOT the detective should claim to be, that means we've got the detective and a sorcerer. Like I said before, one for one is a good deal. There are only 2 sorcs this time.

Or we could wait, the bodyguard could guess one of the 2 to protect and see if he guessed right. The detective should be the highest priority target for the sorcs, so they should try to kill him right away. If they bodyguard guesses right, then we'll know which one the real detective is, we can lynch the sorcerer who was pretending and still have our detective alive. If he guesses wrong, then the detective should be killed that night, then we know who one of the sorcs is and we can lynch them the next day.

Or case number three, we wait, the sorcs kill someone other than the detective, and we've still got two people pretending to be detectives. Not sure what to do in this case. It depends on what the two people say.

But basically, the best bet is to kill them both.

Of course this all depends on a sorc being stupid enough to claim that he's the detective. This is unlikely and the above plan is likely to be unnecessary.

What's for more likely to happen is that the one real detective steps forward. The bodyguard protects him, and he's free to investigate and report the results without having to worry about being killed or being distrusted.

Quote: Kablizzy, 2006-02-23T03:28:48Z
If you seriously believe that the worst thing about pot is that it can land you in jail, you need to take some classes in addiction medicine. I've seen 60 years of Addiction Medicine research that's backing the status of Marijuana's current legality; You're telling me you've seen none of that?

Ive seen some research on the issue. Im not sure if Ive seen the Addiction medicine research though. Im not sure if this is what the topic at hand is, but marijuana is not addictive. Or rather, its addictive in the same way that gambling is addictive to some people. Psychologically.

The bottom line is people with predilection to addiction get addicted. They get addicted to a great variety of things. You cant base laws around those sorts of people. You have to do your best to find ways to help them out while still preserving the rights for the vast majority of non addictive users.

Now, onto the detriments of marijuana!

Quote
One study has indicated have indicated that a users risk of heart attack more than quadruples in the first hour after smoking marijuana(8). The researchers suggest that such an effect might occur from marijuanas effects on blood pressure and heart rate and reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of blood.


Quote
A study of 450 individuals found that people who smoke marijuana frequently but do not smoke tobacco have more health problems and miss more days of work than nonsmokers(9). Many of the extra sick days among the marijuana smokers in the study were for respiratory illnesses.

Even infrequent use can cause burning and stinging of the mouth and throat, often accompanied by a heavy cough. Someone who smokes marijuana regularly may have many of the same respiratory problems that tobacco smokers do, such as daily cough and phlegm production, more frequent acute chest illness, a heightened risk of lung infections, and a greater tendency to obstructed airways(10). Smoking marijuana increases the likelihood of developing cancer of the head or neck, and the more marijuana smoked the greater the increase(11). A study comparing 173 cancer patients and 176 healthy individuals produced strong evidence that marijuana smoking doubled or tripled the risk of these cancers.

Marijuana use also has the potential to promote cancer of the lungs and other parts of the respiratory tract because it contains irritants and carcinogens(12, 13). In fact, marijuana smoke contains 50 to 70 percent more carcinogenic hydrocarbons than does tobacco smoke(14). It also produces high levels of an enzyme that converts certain hydrocarbons into their carcinogenic formlevels that may accelerate the changes that ultimately produce malignant cells(15). Marijuana users usually inhale more deeply and hold their breath longer than tobacco smokers do, which increases the lungs exposure to carcinogenic smoke. These facts suggest that, puff for puff, smoking marijuana may increase the risk of cancer more than smoking tobacco.

These both are the result of smoking marijuana. Unlike cigarettes marijuana has other methods of ingestion, and it seems highly likely that were marijuana made legal that these other safer methods would become much more widely used.

Marijuana smoke is more harmful that cigarette smoke, yes. From what Ive read its about twice as harmful. However I think we can all agree that cigarette smokers smoke way WAY more than 2 times the amount of cigarettes than marijuana users smoke marijuana. So that comparison fails. Ultimately smoking marijuana is better for you than smoking cigarettes.

I dont accept these as harms of marijuana, merely harms from the method of ingestion. Take THC in pill form and these harms disappear completely.


Quote
Some of marijuanas adverse health effects may occur because THC impairs the immune systems ability to fight off infectious diseases and cancer. In laboratory experiments that exposed animal and human cells to THC or other marijuana ingredients, the normal disease-preventing reactions of many of the key types of immune cells were inhibited(16). In other studies, mice exposed to THC or related substances were more likely than unexposed mice to develop bacterial infections and tumors(17, 18).

Ok. This one I hadnt heard about. The degree to which the immune system is inhibited, however, is not written about and the increase in likliehood over the normal mice is similarly not stated. Youd think that if there were a serious risk involved that the anti drug crowd would have been pounding this point to death. The fact that theyre not leads me to believe that the increase in risk is about the same as your increased risk of getting cancer by using sweet n low.

Quote: Kablizzy, 2006-02-23T03:28:48Z
And the following relates to Heavy Marijuana Use:

Quote
Depression(19), anxiety(20), and personality disturbances(21) have been associated with marijuana use. Research clearly demonstrates that marijuana has potential to cause problems in daily life or make a persons existing problems worse. Because marijuana compromises the ability to learn and remember information, the more a person uses marijuana the more he or she is likely to fall behind in accumulating intellectual, job, or social skills. Moreover, research has shown that marijuanas adverse impact on memory and learning can last for days or weeks after the acute effects of the drug wear off(22, 23).

Students who smoke marijuana get lower grades and are less likely to graduate from high school, compared with their non-smoking peers(24, 25, 26, 27). A study of 129 college students found that, for heavy users of marijuana (those who smoked the drug at least 27 of the preceding 30 days), critical skills related to attention, memory, and learning were significantly impaired even after they had not used the drug for at least 24 hours(28). The heavy marijuana users in the study had more trouble sustaining and shifting their attention and in registering, organizing, and using information than did the study participants who had used marijuana no more than 3 of the previous 30 days. As a result, someone who smokes marijuana every day may be functioning at a reduced intellectual level all of the time.

More recently, the same researchers showed that the ability of a group of long-term heavy marijuana users to recall words from a list remained impaired for a week after quitting, but returned to normal within 4 weeks(29). Thus, it is possible that some cognitive abilities may be restored in individuals who quit smoking marijuana, even after long-term heavy use.

Workers who smoke marijuana are more likely than their coworkers to have problems on the job. Several studies associate workers marijuana smoking with increased absences, tardiness, accidents, workers compensation claims, and job turnover. A study of municipal workers found that those who used marijuana on or off the job reported more withdrawal behaviorssuch as leaving work without permission, daydreaming, spending work time on personal matters, and shirking tasksthat adversely affect productivity and morale(30). In another study, marijuana users reported that use of the drug impaired several important measures of life achievement including cognitive abilities, career status, social life, and physical and mental health(31).

Heres my problem with these. Theres no way to prove any sort of causal relationship between marijuana and these problems. It seems to me that its much more likely that due to marijuanas illegal status, the sort of people inclined toward marijuana use are those who already have these sorts of personal issues. How do you factor out the situational bias?

Also, heavy users of pretty much anything experience all sorts of problems. I bet heavy coffee users have all sorts of increased risks for heart disease and personality disorders and all that jazz.
Quote: Kablizzy, 2006-02-23T03:28:48Z
On Pregnancy:

Quote
Research has shown that babies born to women who used marijuana during their pregnancies display altered responses to visual stimuli, increased tremulousness, and a high-pitched cry, which may indicate neurological problems in development(32). During infancy and preschool years, marijuana-exposed children have been observed to have more behavioral problems than unexposed children and poorer performance on tasks of visual perception, language comprehension, sustained attention, and memory(33, 34). In school, these children are more likely to exhibit deficits in decision-making skills, memory, and the ability to remain attentive(35, 36, 37).

Let's begin there. Also, splitting this topic shortly.

I cant say for sure, but I very highly suspect that these issues are a result of the smoke, not the marijuana itself.

This is the problem with this debate. There is tons upon tons of misinformation, misleading studies, intellectually dishonest facts and agenda driven propaganda out there on both sides. I will modify my original claim. Marijuana does have some harmful effects. However, I am positive that the health risks from marijuana are miniscule. On par with eating Macdonalds. Id like to know to what degree you think marijuana is harmful.

March 15th: Keron Cyst is Exhausted



March 18th: Sweep Has Typhoid! Oh no! But I refuse to be slowed down! Onward at the grueling pace!



March 24th: Keron gets better. Yokatta!



March 28th: Sweep gets better too. Yay!

#7672 1 2006-03-27T00:07:41Z Daddaluma
Final Fantasy 12 came on on the 16th here. I resisted buying it for a whole week, but then I couldn't take it anymore, and I caved in and bought it last Friday. It was just getting so much praise heaped on it that I figured I'd be able to get into it even though it's in Japanese.

I was really wary, because I've bought several other RPGs here, only to give up within the first few hours (or first few minutes with Suikoden 3 ), simply because the language barrier made it nearly impossible to enjoy the game.

I had no idea how much my enjoyment of a game comes from being able to understand it effortlesssly. Even action games like God of War and Ratchet and Clank are drastically less fun than their english counterparts.

However, like I said, I could resist and I bought it. I've played it for about 20 hours or so (I've logged 40 hours cause I forgot to turn it off overnight), and I was a bit skeptical at first, but I'm really starting to get into this game. The battle system is a quite radical departure from past Final Fantasy conventions, but it's a most welcome change. No more random battles at all. In fact, no more battle screen at all. It's not even like Crono Trigger where you can see the enemies and when you get into a fight the battle menus come up and it plays out like a normal RPG battle. This is pretty much real time fighting here.

I haven't played many MMORPGs, but I'm told that the fighting is very similar to them. You see an enemy on the screen, you walk up to it and your character will begin to attack it. There's an action bar which fills up, and when it's full your character will attack, and the bar will reset and begin filling up again. You're free to move about and run away (literally run away), you can interupt your character at any time and give him new orders, like item or magic. You only control one character at a time, but you can have 3 members active in battle at one time. The two you don't control will attack continuously, and you can customize their AI through the "gambit" system (sort of like a rudimentary programming language actually) After 20 hours, I am really digging this game's battle system.

And also, after 20 hours, the story is beginning to pick up and I'm getting intrigued. It definitely starts out slow, but there are a ton of hints that everything's going to get alot more complex and involving. In terms of plot, and this is the highest possible praise I can levy upon a game, FF12 is similar to FF Tactics. It's obstensibly about a war, but the war is only the front for one side to gain these immensley powerful god stones.

So that's all I've got at the moment. If you want more in depth reviews and pictures and movies and stuff check out the major game sites. All of them have got some good preview coverage.

Edit: I commited my own pet peeve . . . I used an acronym for a game's name without ever saying the game's name first. God I hate when people do that.

I think Tsukatu's point was this:

1)If an absolutely (ie one unconfined by not only the laws of physics, but the laws of logic) omnipotent deity exists , then it is all-knowing, meaning it can predict the future with 100% accuracy.
2)If the future can be predicted with 100% accuracy, then free will can not exist. The 'choices' we make are predetermined, predictable by physical (and metaphysical, if they exist) laws
3)Therefore if an absolutely omnipotent deity exists, then free will cannot. At least, human free will cannot exist - the deity will be the sole possesor of free will.

Therefore an ablolutely omnipotent God and the existence of human free will are mutually exclusive.

Now thats a good solid argument. I assume were all on board and that this is exactly the point that Tsukatu was getting at in the beginning, right?

Now I dont know where to begin. There are a lot of things I want to say and I dont know which to say first. Eh, Ill actually be patient for once in my life and go through the issues one by one. Lets start with a deist defense.

The argument above uses temporal terms like predict and future with regards to an omnipotent and omniscient being. But if we set God outside of time, then these words dont have any meaning and this argument gets really slippery. If God is outside of time, then he cant be said to be predicting our futures. All of our time is one big instant to him. All of our time happens in the same instant. All of the choices we make, and all of the results of those choices are all simultaneous to an extemporal God. So our future isnt determined. God only knows what happens because he is seeing what we will choose right now.

Now Gods knowledge is no different than our own. If I watch you choose coffee over orange juice, I know what you chose because I watched you choose. I dont see how this act of watching can be said to determine your choice. God knows you choose coffee because hes watching you choose coffee. It just so happens that at the very same instant god is watching absolutely everything that will ever happen, but Im not sure that really changes things.

Anyway, there you have it. That's one possible way to defeat this argument. I'll let this one run its course and then present another.
